idea: firms issue shares when they are overvalued and buy them back when undervalued; investors under-react to these managerial signals, so net issuers underperform and repurchasers outperform for years (one-year window, Pontiff-Woodgate horizon).
rationale_data: cap and returns (price-volume data, every region): market value growth not explained by returns is net issuance minus payouts
rationale_operators: log(cap / ts_delay(cap, k)) - ts_sum(log(1 + returns), k) is the composite issuance of Daniel-Titman; the minus sign shorts issuers and buys repurchasers

idea: firms issue shares when they are overvalued and buy them back when undervalued; investors under-react to these managerial signals, so net issuers underperform and repurchasers outperform for years (five-year window, Daniel-Titman horizon; FIN uses both).
rationale_data: cap and returns (price-volume data, every region): market value growth not explained by returns is net issuance minus payouts
rationale_operators: log(cap / ts_delay(cap, k)) - ts_sum(log(1 + returns), k) is the composite issuance of Daniel-Titman; the minus sign shorts issuers and buys repurchasers

expression: rank(add(ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 231), 21), ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 483), 21), ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 735), 21), ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 987), 21), ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 1239), 21), filter=true))
idea: stocks tend to outperform in the same calendar month in which they outperformed in earlier years (earnings announcement timing, fiscal-year flows and recurring demand): the next month's return in each of the last five years predicts this year's.
rationale_operators: ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 231 + 252k), 21) is the return over the coming month k+1 years ago; add(..., filter=true) averages the five years and keeps stocks with shorter histories

expression: rank(ts_mean(if_else(open > ts_delay(close, 1), if_else(close < open, 1, 0), 0), 21) / ts_mean(ts_mean(if_else(open > ts_delay(close, 1), if_else(close < open, 1, 0), 0), 21), 252))
idea: a month with many days of overnight gains followed by daytime losses is a tug of war between overnight noise traders and daytime arbitrageurs; the arbitrageurs over-correct a persistent overnight price pressure, so the most intense tug of war predicts higher returns.
rationale_data: open and close (price-volume data, every region): the overnight return is open over the previous close, the daytime return close over open
rationale_operators: if_else marks days with a positive overnight and a negative daytime return; ts_mean over 21 days is the month's frequency, divided by its own 12-month average as in the paper; rank orders stocks

idea: analysts' target-price-implied returns are informative relative to industry peers: ranking target price over price within an industry removes analysts' industry-wide optimism and keeps their relative valuation.
rationale_data: consensus analyst target price and the close price
rationale_operators: ts_backfill(target, 63) / close is the implied return; group_rank within the industry

idea: the same relative valuation with the vendor's bias-free target price, which removes each analyst's systematic optimism before averaging.
rationale_data: bias-free average price target and the close price
rationale_operators: ts_backfill(target, 63) / close ranked within the industry

idea: investors fail to separate bold revisions (away from consensus, new information) from herding ones; the drift after bold upward minus bold downward revisions is the under-priced part of analysts' news.
rationale_data: counts of positive and negative bold FY1 earnings estimates
rationale_operators: ts_backfill carries the counts over a quarter; rank of their difference

idea: uncertainty about risk is disliked: stocks whose implied volatility itself is volatile (high vol-of-vol) underperform those with stable implied volatility, by about 8% a year in the U.S. and Europe.
rationale_data: at-the-money call and put implied volatility (opt3, used in submitted composites #493 / #499)
rationale_operators: ts_std_dev over ts_mean of the 21-day ATM implied volatility is its coefficient of variation; ts_backfill(…, 5) bridges missing days; the minus sign shorts high vol-of-vol

idea: the same vol-of-vol on the 30-day at-the-money call volatility of the option horizon dataset, whose fields few BRAIN alphas use.
rationale_data: 30-day at-the-money call implied volatility (option horizon decomposition)
rationale_operators: coefficient of variation of the 21-day implied volatility; the minus sign shorts high vol-of-vol

idea: prices under-react to firm news: the return on days with news keeps drifting in the same direction for several days, without reversal, more so when investors are distracted.
rationale_data: returns and the RavenPack story vector (nws18_ssc: one entry per story)
rationale_operators: if_else keeps the returns of days with at least one story; ts_sum over 5 days; returns of no-news days, which reverse, are left out
